quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
rationale: Section 15.1 gives us an express MSL duty to protect, defend and indemnify IBM against third-party claims, expressly including IP infringement by MSL's performance, procured Parts, processes, designs, deliverables and contributed pre-existing material (p0260), plus MSL's failure to comply with law (p0261). Exclusions are narrow and Vendor-standard (IBM written specifications/designs, IBM-selected marks), and Section 15.2 carries the usual procedure: prompt written notice, cooperation, and MSL control of the defence with IBM participation at its option (p0266-p0268). Section 15.2(b) also gives the procure-a-licence / non-infringing substitute remedy (p0271). This meets the fallback on its material terms and most of the preferred position, so we would not redline it. Noted but not flagged: (i) the p0271 remedy is at MSL's discretion and there is no express refund if no cure is available, though MSL's damages indemnity is unqualified; (ii) the indemnity runs to IBM only (Attachment 6 App. A section 5 extends to IBM Subsidiaries) and does not separately name data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers - preferred-only sub-elements; (iii) no indemnity super-cap is imposed, which favours us, although the general 3% cap in Section 15.3(b) is written without an indemnity carve-out and is being handled under the limitation-of-liability rule rather than flagged twice here. There is no IBM indemnity in favour of MSL; Section 14 of the Loan Agreement is a narrow IBM patent obligation limited to IBM-supplied Loaned Items, so our side stays narrow.

quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
rationale:
The IP bargain runs in our favour and meets the preferred position on its material terms. Section 13.1 (p0197) gives IBM ownership of, and MSL a present and future assignment of, all intellectual and industrial property rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered; p0198 extends IBM ownership/MSL assignment to MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes and systems, with MSL's retained use limited to performing its obligations here. Ownership is stronger than the fallback licence, so the fallback licence elements (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use, modification and sublicensing) are subsumed. MSL keeps generic production tooling (p1088: "Tools commonly used in production and/or Integration will be owned and managed by MSL"), which the playbook expressly permits. Any MSL licence in IBM information is confined to service delivery: 13.3(a) (p0208) grants MSL only a royalty-free licence to use confidential information disclosed under the AECI "necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM", and any other licence to IBM IP requires a separate signed agreement; IBM documentation and confidential media must be returned on termination (p0130). There is no joint ownership and no assignment of IBM IP or data to MSL, so no walk-away trigger. Minor points noted only, not redlined: there is no express "MSL retains its pre-existing IP" sentence (a Vendor-side omission that does not prejudice us), no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence, and 24.1(a) (p1136) says MSL conveys no licence under its own IP in the I/T systems context, which is overridden for delivered Products by the 13.1 assignment. The AECI residuals clause (p1482) is a confidentiality mechanic reviewed under that rule, not IP.</rationale>
</invoke>

Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.

mappings.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 16.2 bars assignment by IBM without MSL's approval with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, which is our walk-away position. We have added the customary IBM affiliate/successor rights, confirmed that an IBM change of control gives MSL no termination right, and kept MSL's assignments subject to IBM's approval (not unreasonably withheld) and off-limits to our competitors.

ops.text: IBM may assign this Agreement without MSL's approval to an affiliate of IBM or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, and no change of control of IBM shall give MSL any right to terminate this Agreement. MSL may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of IBM, and IBM's approval of any other assignment by MSL shall not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, no MSL termination on IBM change of control, bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and a reasonableness standard on IBM's approval of other MSL assignments.

quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM.
rationale: Section 16.2 imposes a blanket prohibition on assignment by IBM without MSL's prior written approval, with no affiliate carve-out and no successor/M&A carve-out, and no reasonableness standard on MSL's approval of an IBM assignment. That is our walk-away position and fails the fallback as well (no successor assignment right on written notice for either party). The only reasonableness standard runs in MSL's favour, for assignments to an MSL Related Company. Section 16.5 (p0290) helpfully requires any acquirer of MSL to assume the Agreement, and the Loan Agreement general clause (p1578) restricts MSL only, so neither is flagged. There is no change-of-control termination right anywhere in the document, but nothing affirmatively confirms this, so we state it expressly. Our single inserted sentence pair cures the Customer-side carve-outs at the preferred level while leaving MSL's assignments subject to IBM's approval; MSL's existing prohibition already satisfies the Vendor-consent element.

elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "IBM may assign this Agreement without MSL's approval to an affiliate of IBM ..." — a direct no-approval permission for Customer affiliate transfers.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence continues "... or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" without MSL's approval, tracking the checklist triggers verbatim.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Retained operative text: "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM." Also reinforced by the retained mutual first sentence.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "IBM's approval of any other assignment by MSL shall not be unreasonably withheld," which, read with the retained Related-Company sentence ("not be unreasonably withheld or delayed"), covers MSL assignments generally.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "MSL may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of IBM" — an unconditional prohibition, not subject to a consent cure.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "no change of control of IBM shall give MSL any right to terminate this Agreement"; no contrary change-of-control termination right appears in the cited text.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only IBM receives a successor transfer right; MSL remains barred ("MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties ... without prior written approval by IBM"). Section 16.5 only obliges an MSL acquirer to assume the Agreement; it grants MSL no assignment right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted permission contains no notice obligation; the only notice duty is MSL's immediate notice of a sale/merger under the retained 16.5 sentence, which is not a successor-assignment notice condition.

elements.element: Other assignments require consent.
elements.evidence: The insertion creates a standing no-consent exception for IBM affiliate transfers (a non-successor exception), which defeats the fallback requirement that all other assignments run through consent.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is one-directional: it governs only "any other assignment by MSL." Any IBM assignment outside the affiliate/successor carve-out still needs MSL's "prior written approval" with no reasonableness qualifier.

verification.notes: All six preferred elements are met in operative language: the two-sentence insertion supplies the Customer affiliate and merger/acquisition/substantially-all-assets carve-outs, the competitor bar, the reasonableness standard on IBM's approval of MSL assignments, and the express no-change-of-control-termination confirmation, while the retained sentence "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM" already carries the Vendor-consent element. Fallback is incomplete (no MSL successor right, no written-notice condition, a retained no-consent affiliate exception, and no mutual reasonableness standard), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation since the as-drafted clause failed the fallback on material terms. Minimality holds: nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased, the favourable retained language (mutual approval sentence, MSL Related Company reasonableness, subcontractor disclosure, 16.5 successor-assumption warranty) survives intact, and the drafter used a direct "without MSL's approval" permission rather than a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause. No survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure was added. Intent is preserved: the added permission operates as a specific exception to the retained general "Neither Party may assign ... without prior written approval" sentence rather than contradicting it, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling. Minor drafting point (not a defect requiring repair): "any other assignment by MSL" sits alongside the retained MSL Related Company consent sentence, so consider confirming that the competitor prohibition overrides a Related Company transfer to an IBM competitor if that risk is live.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

quote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-source or requirements obligation on IBM. The purchase clause (§ 6.0, p0720) is order-driven and expressly conditioned on Purchase Orders ("This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product"), with IBM free to cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time (§ 6.1, p0722). The Scope of Work (§ 3.0, p0102) covers only "selected" manufacturing and Services. The only "exclusive" references are unrelated (entire-agreement wording in p1500, exclusive remedy in p1574, and secure media storage in p1341). Section 9.0(e) (p0186) affirmatively contemplates "reductions of Products requirements due to migration to a competitive supplier", confirming our freedom to source elsewhere; it only allocates severance cost, which is not a restrictive covenant. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.

mappings.quote: For any calendar month, if MSL fails to achieve a responsiveness, as defined in Appendix 3, of at least [*]% for any machine type, in a Work Center, a penalty of [*]% will be applied to that Work Center's monthly total material cost of that machine type

quote: For any calendar month, if MSL fails to achieve a responsiveness, as defined in Appendix 3, of at least [*]% for any machine type, in a Work Center, a penalty of [*]% will be applied to that Work Center's monthly total material cost of that machine type multiplied by ([*]% minus actual responsiveness %).
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by IBM, so it meets the preferred position. The only penalty and payment-adjustment mechanics run against MSL and in our favour: the responsiveness penalty (p0757) and the delinquent-shipment profit-rate adjustments (p0749-p0756, p0418-p0419). Purchase Order cancellation is at IBM's discretion with no cancellation charge on MSL default (p0722), and the only amounts IBM pays on cancellation or termination are cost reimbursements and negotiated prices for completed/partially completed Products and Parts (Sections 5.2-5.3, p0131-p0143), which are consideration for goods rather than a liquidated sum. Payment terms in Sections 6.1-6.2 impose no late-payment interest or penalty on IBM. No redline is warranted.

quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
rationale: No licence runs from MSL (Vendor) to IBM (Customer) that could be revocable or exclude our affiliates/contractors. Instead, Section 13.1 vests outright ownership in IBM by assignment of all IP in the hardware, software, design and documentation of Products, and 13.2 confirms IBM receives no MSL confidential information; Section 13.0's only reservation to MSL (p0198) is a narrow right to use assigned inventions in performing its own obligations, plus a bar on MSL injecting proprietary processes. Ownership exceeds every preferred element: it is inherently perpetual, irrevocable, not terminable at MSL's discretion, and freely transferable to IBM's successors, and it lets IBM extend rights to contractors (reinforced by 5.2(a)(ii), under which MSL must transfer responsibilities and Products "to IBM or to another party that IBM designates"). Affiliate coverage is already built in: clause 1.9 defines "IBM" as International Business Machines Corporation "and its Subsidiaries", so adding affiliate wording would be duplicative. The licences in 13.3(a), the Loan Agreement (Sections 5 and 6) and Attachment 6 run from IBM to MSL and are restrictions on the Vendor that benefit us, so they are not flagged. The mutual sentence in 24.1(a) that "MSL conveys to IBM no software title or license under the intellectual property rights of MSL or of any third party" is a reciprocal no-implied-licence statement in the I/T system-access context, not a grant clause, and does not cut into IBM's ownership of Product IP. The only wording short of the preferred template is the absence of an express "contractors acting on IBM's behalf" phrase, which is a drafting nicety here rather than a material gap given IBM's ownership; noted, not redlined.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 1) providing to others products or services which may be competitive with products or services of the Discloser; 2) providing products or services to others who compete with the Discloser; or 3) assigning its employees in any way it may choose.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on IBM, so it sits at our preferred position. Searches for compete/competing, exclusivity, field-of-use, territory, sole-source and requirements language returned no covenant binding IBM. The only competition-related provisions run the other way or are neutral: (i) the confidentiality terms at p1490-p1491 expressly preserve each recipient's freedom to provide competitive products or services and to assign employees as it chooses; (ii) Section 5.1(b)(v) (p0116) is a mutual change-of-control termination trigger, not a restraint on the businesses IBM may operate; and (iii) Section 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations" (p0995) restricts MSL's use of IBM property, which benefits us. The Attachment 1 Section 7.4 mechanics (p0767-p0775) are disclosure/right-to-match provisions that expressly permit IBM to move Product to the third party if MSL cannot match; that is MFN territory, not exclusivity, and is not flagged here. No redline required.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5.0 today allows exit only for cause, leaving us locked into a three-year term, so we have added Section 5.4 under which IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience on thirty (30) days' prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" opener keeps the for-cause rights intact while ensuring that preamble is not read as an exclusive list; we can move to 60-90 days' notice as our fallback.

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience by IBM. Notwithstanding Section 5.1, IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 5.4: IBM convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, prevailing over the Section 5.1 for-cause preamble

quote: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable. IBM's termination of Purchase Orders for its convenience shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section.
rationale: The only convenience mechanic in the deal is the quoted SOW Section 6.1, which reaches individual Purchase Orders and still leaves IBM liable for cost reimbursements; it does not let IBM exit the Agreement. The Base Agreement runs three years (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause - breach, insolvency, competitor acquisition, or continuing force majeure (p0107 to p0118). Section 4.0's six-month notice is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL, not T4C). Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is a missing-behaviour deviation, so we insert operative language: 'IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL', with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. I re-checked the cross-reference: the retained for-cause preamble sits under the heading paragraph '5.1 Breach' (p0106), so 'Notwithstanding Section 5.1' is not dangling; that narrow opener avoids rewriting Section 5.1. Direction is checked - MSL has no mid-term convenience right, so preferred element 4 is already met and no new restriction on MSL is drafted. 60 to 90 days' notice remains the fallback concession.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 5.4: "IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL". The element is disjunctive, so a right reaching the Agreement itself suffices; the pre-existing PO cancellation right (p0722) is additional, not required. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returns false only because the rendered phrasing is "terminate this Agreement for its convenience" (interposed "its"); in substance the operative right is present and runs in Customer's favour.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" - 30 days, written, no additional conditions or Vendor consent.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination" - the word "pro rata" is express, not inferred from the post-termination period alone, and the payer direction is Vendor-to-Customer.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 5.1 preamble limits exit to cause: "this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows", and Section 4.0 permits termination during the initial three-year term only "as provided in Section 5.0". Section 4.0's six (6) months' notice operates against automatic renewal and is scored under RENEWAL, not as a mid-term Vendor convenience right. The new 5.4 grants the convenience right to IBM only and creates no reciprocal MSL right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 sets thirty (30) days, which is better than fallback but outside the 60-90 day band; the fallback level is therefore not the level satisfied.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No fee cap appears anywhere; the retained cost-reimbursement mechanics (p0722 "shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section" and the Parts cost provision at p0143) remain uncapped. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to add an express cap of three (3) months' fees on any charge payable on convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.0 lets "either Party" give six (6) months' written notice "of its intent to terminate this Agreement" without expressly tying the effective date to the end of the then-current renewal term; per the rule boundary, such an auto-renewal notice mechanic does not establish term-end-only Vendor termination. (Immaterial here because the preferred level is complete.)

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition is effectively inapplicable: MSL has no mid-term convenience right, and the only notice-based exit available to MSL (Section 4.0) requires six (6) months' notice, comfortably exceeding 90 days.

verification.notes: Customer convenience termination present: failed Position-complete at the preferred level: the inserted Section 5.4 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and the retained for-cause-only Section 5.0 already denies MSL any mid-term convenience exit, so no new restriction on MSL was needed or drafted. Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no survival tail, expense allocation, damages category, or procedure is bolted on, and the T4C-surplus phrase "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted since the selected checklist and the Agreement's Purchase Order cancellation right (p0722) do not require a partial-termination structure. The narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" opener is justified rather than a broad override: Section 5.1's own preamble reads "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows", which would otherwise contradict the new clause. The reference resolves to the heading at p0106, so it is not dangling. Intent preserved: the for-cause grounds, the three-year term, the Section 4.0 renewal/non-renewal mechanic, the Purchase Order cancellation right, and the Parts cost-reimbursement pricing (p0143) all survive without contradiction, because the override is limited to Section 5.1. Residual point to verify before sending (not a defect in the drafted language): confirm that "5.4" is an unused number within Section 5.0, which appears to run through several subsections (p0107-p0118); renumber if it collides. Note for negotiation, not a checklist failure: retained p0722 and the Parts cost provision mean a convenience exit may still carry cost reimbursements. If the counterparty pushes us to the fallback (60-90 days), we would then also need an express cap of three (3) months' fees on those charges to make the fallback level complete.

quote: a) IBM may perform process audits at MSL's or an MSL Related Company's Work Center or MSL's subcontractors' facilities to assure that identified IBM specifications have been complied with.
rationale: Every audit, inspection and verification right in the Agreement runs in our favour, not against us: Section 7.0 process audits (p0163-p0164), Attachment 6 Section 4.0 software-location monitoring/inspection/audit (p1310-p1314), Attachment 6 Section 4 books-and-records audits and inspections of MSL and its Subsidiaries (p1443, at MSL's facilities, 45 days' written notice, independent CPA, MSL pays only if material discrepancies are disclosed) (p1448), consigned inventory and tooling inspections, and acceptance/source inspection. Section 16.14 Records is a mutual record-retention obligation only and confers no examination right over IBM. MSL has no right to audit, inspect or access IBM's records, facilities or systems anywhere in the document, so there is no audit exposure against the Customer to limit — the position is better than the preferred checklist (no frequency, notice, cost or system-access constraints are needed because no Vendor audit right exists). Nothing to redline; flagging the IBM-favourable audit rights would weaken our own position.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: This Agreement and the performance of transactions under this Agreement shall be governed by the substantive laws of the state of New York.
rationale: Section 16.9 selects New York substantive law (p0300) and requires any action related to a breach to be commenced "in a court sited within the State of New York" (p0301), which is a mandatory judicial forum in an accepted jurisdiction covering both state and federal courts sited in New York. The subordinate documents are consistent: the AECI general clause (p1499) and Loan Agreement Section 16 (p1587) also select New York law. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the document and no foreign venue, so the walk-away scenario is not present. This meets the accepted-law/courts parameter at the preferred level rather than merely the fallback (Delaware, California, or England and Wales). Two minor points short of the preferred wording are noted but not redlined: the venue is New York State generally rather than expressly New York County, and exclusivity is expressed through the mandatory "must be commenced ... in a court sited within the State of New York" formulation rather than the words "exclusive jurisdiction". The mutual jury-trial waiver and the contractual limitations period in p0300-p0301 are separate commercial terms outside this rule and are mutual in effect.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: MSL agrees that MSL engineering will be priced to IBM on a "most favored customer" basis.
rationale: The only most-favoured-nation mechanic in the Agreement runs in our favour: MSL must price its engineering to IBM on a "most favored customer" basis (p1099). Targeted searches for reciprocal language ("no less favorable", "more favorable terms", "best price", "favorable", "match", "preferential", "lowest") return nothing that obliges IBM to extend MSL terms given to third parties. The adjacent right-to-match on tooling (p1104) and the right of first refusal (p1230) likewise benefit IBM, and MSL's low-cost purchasing undertaking (p0821) is a Vendor obligation. This meets the preferred position — Customer has no MFN obligation benefiting Vendor — so no redline is proposed and the Vendor-granted MFN is retained.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
rationale: There is no take-or-pay or minimum volume obligation on us. Forecasts expressly "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product" (p0882); Products are "produced and delivered according to actual intake of IBM Customer Orders" and the forecast is only MSL's Parts-ordering authorisation (p0870); we may "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (p0722); and "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility" under the Supply Flexibility appendix (p0927). The only volume-linked exposure is the Requirements Accuracy mechanic (p0903 / Appendix 2): we bear no liability for MSL's inventory while forecast accuracy stays at or above the Appendix 2 level, and below it we compensate MSL by applying stated percentages to the actual material cost of the affected machine type. That is a cost true-up for materials MSL actually procured on our forecast, not a shortfall penalty or a multi-year commitment, and we retain an unconditional exit via PO cancellation — so the bargain sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Worth noting in the rationale only (not as a deviation): the Appendix 2 percentages and thresholds are redacted, so we should confirm on the business side that the incremental percentage is genuinely cost-recovery and not punitive, and that MSL's inventory exposure remains limited to Parts within published lead times (p0870) and the Supply Flexibility window.

The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
mappings.quote: in any way solicit for employment any

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept only a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the work and running 12 months from the end of that involvement, so we have narrowed the restriction accordingly and conformed the retained unsolicited-approach and general solicitation/employment advertising carve-outs to apply to either party and to the new scope wording; the solicitation-only (no no-hire) formulation is unchanged.

ops.newText: Neither party will, for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in performing this Agreement, in any way solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party
ops.oldText: IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date of this Agreement, it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees without the prior written consent of MSL

ops.newText: the foregoing will not restrict or prevent either party from a) employing any such person who contacts that party on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from that party or b) by using general solicitation or general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto, provided that such party does not direct or encourage such independent search firms to solicit such personnel.
ops.oldText: the foregoing will not restrict or prevent IBM from a) employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM or b) by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto, provided that IBM does not direct or encourage such independent search firms to solicit such Transferred Employees.

proposal.summary: Make the Section 9.0(f) non-solicit mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in performing the Agreement, cap it at 12 months after that involvement ends, and conform the retained unsolicited-contact and general solicitation/advertising carve-outs so they apply to either party and track the new scope wording.

quote: f) IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date of this Agreement, it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees without the prior written consent of MSL; provided, however, that the foregoing will not restrict or prevent IBM from a) employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM or b) by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto
rationale: Section 9.0(f) is the only non-solicitation provision in the Agreement and it binds IBM alone. It fails the fallback on three material terms: it is one-sided rather than mutual; it covers every Transferred Employee regardless of involvement in performing this Agreement; and it runs for "[*] years" from the Effective Date rather than 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement. It prohibits solicitation only and expressly permits hiring, so there is no no-hire. Operation 1 makes the restriction mutual, limits it to the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement and caps it at 12 months after that involvement ends; operation 2 conforms the retained carve-outs so they excuse either party, states the general solicitation/employment advertising exclusion expressly, and replaces the now-dangling "such Transferred Employees" with "such personnel". Note for the client: the involvement-based scope re-cuts rather than uniformly narrows the covered population.

elements.element: Customer has no non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The rendered Section 9.0(f) retains a solicitation restriction binding on both parties ("Neither party will ... in any way solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement"). Customer (IBM), which was the only restricted party in the original, remains restricted, so the preferred no-restriction outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: The non-solicitation restriction is mutual.
elements.evidence: "Neither party will ... solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel ... without the prior written consent of the other party" — the one-sided "IBM agrees that ... it will not" formulation and the MSL-only consent right are replaced with reciprocal wording, and the carve-outs are conformed to "that party"/"such party".

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Covered population is narrowed from "any Transferred Employees" to "any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement"; the dangling "such Transferred Employees" in the search-firm proviso is conformed to "such personnel". In this outsourcing agreement the Services are the work performed under the Agreement, so "directly involved in performing this Agreement" tracks the element.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in performing this Agreement" replaces "for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date"; both the length (12 months) and the temporal anchor (end of involvement) match the element.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained and conformed limb (b): "by using general solicitation or general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto" — general advertising is expressly excluded (the original "general employment advertising or communications" already covered this).

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained and conformed limb (a): "employing any such person who contacts that party on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from that party".

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is solicitation only — "in any way solicit for employment" — and both carve-outs expressly permit "employing"/"hiring" the person; no "employ or engage" or no-hire language is introduced or retained.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: the rendered clause is mutual, scoped to personnel directly involved in performing the Agreement, capped at 12 months from the end of that involvement, retains the unsolicited-approach and general-advertising carve-outs, and prohibits solicitation only (no no-hire). Position-complete at the fallback level. Preferred level is not met and cannot be, because the redline retains a restriction binding Customer (IBM). That is an acceptable choice given the finding targets the fallback, but the comment should make clear to the client that Customer remains restricted where it previously was the only restricted party. Edits are confined to the four items the fallback requires (mutuality, scope, duration/anchor, conforming the carve-outs and the now-dangling "such Transferred Employees" reference). No survival tail, expense, procedure or extra obligation is added, and the favourable existing search-firm proviso and consent mechanic are retained. Minor trim available without affecting completeness: the inserted words "general solicitation or" are not strictly necessary, since the retained "general employment advertising or communications" already satisfied the general-advertisement element. Treated as de minimis conforming language rather than a minimality failure, but the drafter could delete it to keep the redline tightest. Intent preserved: no undefined term or dangling cross-reference results — "Transferred Employees" remains defined elsewhere and is simply no longer used in this clause, consent is reciprocated to "the other party", and no other allocation, timing or commercial mechanic in Section 9.0 is contradicted. Note on scope re-cut (correctly flagged in the rationale): moving from "Transferred Employees" to "personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement" narrows in some respects and broadens in others (e.g., Vendor personnel never transferred are now covered against Customer solicitation). This tracks the playbook fallback, so it is not a defect, but confirm the client accepts the re-cut.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The six-month (Base Agreement) and twelve-month (Attachment) non-renewal notice windows are far longer than our 60-day fallback, and the Attachment's twelve-month notice exceeds its own six-month renewal term. We have shortened both windows to sixty days; renewals otherwise continue on the same terms and conditions, so pricing remains unchanged.
proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice to 60 days in Base Agreement §4.0 and Attachment §2.0

quote: This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement. Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.
rationale: Both renewal clauses auto-renew but impose non-renewal notice windows far beyond the 60-day fallback: Base Agreement §4.0 requires six months (~180 days) against 12-month renewal terms, and Attachment §2.0 requires twelve months (~365 days) against six-month renewal terms, so the Attachment can effectively never be exited at term end. Notice windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory, so this fails the fallback on a material term. Renewal pricing is not a problem: both clauses provide that renewals continue \"under the same terms and conditions\", so no unilateral price increase is permitted and no cap is needed. We therefore make the minimal fallback fix — shortening each notice window to sixty (60) days — rather than upgrading to preferred (30-day opt-out, vendor reminder, CPI cap).

elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Both clauses retain automatic renewal ("will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months" / "six (6) months"), so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied; the 30-day opt-out and the 60-day Vendor reminder are absent, so this gateway element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Base Agreement renews for "periods of twelve (12) months"; the Attachment renews for "periods of six (6) months" — both within 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Both rendered clauses require "sixty (60) days written notice of its intent to terminate" — twice the preferred 30-day opt-out window.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered language; the drafter expressly declined to add one ("rather than upgrading to preferred (30-day opt-out, vendor reminder, CPI cap)").

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewals "shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties," so no unilateral Vendor price increase is permitted — any change needs Customer's written agreement.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Both clauses now read "unless either Party gives sixty (60) days written notice of its intent to terminate" — exactly 60 days in the Base Agreement §4.0 and the Attachment §2.0, replacing the prior six-month and twelve-month windows.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: both clauses preserve "under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties," which bars any unilateral uplift; a cap is therefore unnecessary.

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: both notice windows are reduced to sixty (60) days, and the retained "same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties" language means renewal permits no unilateral price increase, so the 5 percent cap element is satisfied by non-application of its condition. Preferred level is not complete: the 30-day Customer opt-out and the 60-day Vendor pre-renewal reminder are both absent from operative language. To reach preferred the drafter would need to change "sixty (60) days written notice" to "thirty (30) days written notice" for Customer and insert an express Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date. Minimality holds: the only textual change in each paragraph is the numeric notice period ("six (6) months" → "sixty (60) days"; "twelve (12) months" → "sixty (60) days"). Renewal term lengths, the termination cross-references to Section 5.0, the three-year initial term, and the same-terms pricing sentence are all retained verbatim; no extras (reminders, CPI formulas, survival tails) were added beyond the chosen fallback checklist. Intent is preserved: the three-year initial term, Section 5.0 termination rights, Product Attachment incorporation, and the mutual character of the notice right are unchanged, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created. Note for the drafter (not a defect): shortening the mutual window also shortens Vendor's exit notice from six/twelve months to sixty days; if long Vendor-side notice was commercially valuable to us, consider an asymmetric edit shortening only Customer's window while leaving Vendor's longer notice intact. Both edited paragraphs are covered, which is necessary — leaving the Attachment's twelve-month window (against a six-month renewal term, an unexitable structure and walk-away territory) would have left the fallback incomplete.

mappings.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a short exit provision so that transition assistance is available for at least ninety Days after any expiration or termination and our data is exported back to us within thirty Days. This is our fallback transition position; the existing Section 5.2 assistance obligation has no duration and is tied only to default terminations.

ops.text: d) Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, MSL will provide the transition assistance described in Subsection 5.2 a) ii) for a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination, and will, within thirty (30) Days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to IBM all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM that is in MSL's possession or control.

proposal.summary: Insert 90-day transition assistance and 30-day data export obligation on any expiry or termination.

quote: a) Upon the expiration or termination for default of this Agreement, MSL will:
rationale: The only exit-assistance obligation is Section 5.2 a) ii) (\"assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products ... to IBM or to another party that IBM designates\"), which is (i) gated by the chapeau in p0121 to expiration or termination for default rather than any termination, and (ii) has no committed duration, so it fails the fallback requirement of at least 90 days of transition assistance. The return obligation in Section 5.2 a) iii) is limited to IBM Product documentation and confidential media, runs on a redacted \"[*] Days\" period, and is not a data export within a fixed 30 days. Section 12.0/Supplement 1 Transition Services are inbound only (they expired December 31, 1998) and Attachment 6/Section 12.1 cover software master media and Loaned Items, not our data. We therefore inserted the shortest fallback clause: 90 Days of assistance after any expiry or termination plus a 30-Day export of all IBM data. We did not pursue the preferred six-month/then-current-rates/certified-deletion package.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted Subsection 5.2 d): "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, MSL will provide the transition assistance ..." — this cures the chapeau in 5.2 a), which was limited to "expiration or termination for default".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: New clause d) commits only to "a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination"; no six-month assistance period appears anywhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Clause d) is silent on pricing; neither it nor Section 5.2 a) ii) contains any then-current-rates (or any charging) mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d): "within thirty (30) Days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to IBM all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM that is in MSL's possession or control." (Note: "Days" is defined at 1.3 as business days.)

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Clause d) requires only that MSL "export and deliver" the data; no commonly used/machine-readable format requirement is stated, and Section 5.2 a) iii) speaks only of returning documentation and confidential media.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written-certification obligation exists in clause d) or elsewhere in the cited termination provisions.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d) opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason", so the assistance and export duties are not gated to default terminations.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Clause d) fixes the previously open-ended Section 5.2 a) ii) duty: "provide the transition assistance described in Subsection 5.2 a) ii) for a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination."

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d): export and delivery of "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM" within thirty (30) Days after expiration or termination; the scope covers every category of IBM data, not selected types.

verification.notes: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted Subsection 5.2 d) supplies (i) an any-reason trigger, (ii) a committed minimum 90-Day assistance period anchored to the existing Section 5.2 a) ii) assistance scope, and (iii) a 30-Day export of all IBM data. Preferred is not complete — four elements are absent from operative language: a six-month assistance period, a then-current-rates charging basis, a commonly used machine-readable return format, and post-return certified deletion. The finding correctly targets fallback only. Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletion or paraphrase of existing Section 5.2 language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and no duplication of the existing 5.2 a) iii) return of documentation/confidential media (which is a different subject matter). Intent preserved: clause d) supplements rather than contradicts the 5.2 a) default-only chapeau and 5.2 c) inventory buy-back; the cross-reference to "Subsection 5.2 a) ii)" resolves to an existing provision, leaving no dangling reference or undefined term. Drafting caution (not a failure): "Days" is defined at 1.3 as business days, so the 30-Day export window runs roughly six calendar weeks and the 90-Day assistance period runs roughly eighteen calendar weeks. The usage is consistent with Section 5.2 a) iii) and the defined-term convention, but if a hard calendar deadline is wanted, change the export trigger to lower-case "thirty (30) calendar days". Optional strengthening toward preferred, if leverage allows: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export duty and a sentence requiring MSL thereafter to delete IBM data and certify deletion in writing; add "at MSL's then-current rates" only if the parties need an express charging basis.

quote: a) MSL expressly warrants that all Products, MSL supplied materials and Parts, and work prepared for IBM will conform in all material respects to the specifications, drawings, or other descriptions furnished or adopted by IBM, and will be of specified quality, good workmanship, and free from defect subject to the following terms:
rationale: MSL gives an express conformance warranty on all Products, materials, Parts and work prepared for IBM (§19.1(a), p1059), i.e. the deliverable-to-documentation warranty the rule requires, measured against IBM's specifications, drawings and descriptions. Discrete periods are stated for MSL Procured Parts ([*] months, p1063) and for MSL's workmanship ([*] months, p1067) — the workmanship/service leg is expressed in months, comfortably above the 30-day fallback floor — and those periods run from delivery, survive acceptance testing and expressly reach latent defects (p1068). The remedy stack matches the fallback: MSL must complete Failure Analysis, repair or replacement of defective Products and, "If repair or replacement is not possible, MSL will refund to IBM, MSL's price associated with the failed Product" (§19.5, p1077), with defective FRUs returned freight collect (§19.2). The §19.6 disclaimer (p1079) is a conventional implied-warranty exclusion that is expressly "in lieu of" other terms while preserving MSL's Section 19 obligations, so it does not swallow the express warranty; the "AS IS" language at p0174 and p1567 runs against MSL on IBM-supplied assets and loaned items and benefits us. This therefore sits at the fallback and is not redlined. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the numeric warranty periods are redacted ([*] months), so the 90-day software floor cannot be verified on the face of the document; there is no express compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty and no 12-month software period, which are preferred-level refinements only; and §16.19 (p0329) caps the life of the Agreement's representations and warranties at the [*] anniversary of the Effective Date.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

mappings.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no general insurance article even though MSL holds our consigned inventory, works with our premises and accesses our I/T systems, so we added our standard coverage requirements. We can discuss lower E&O and cyber limits if MSL's programme is constrained.

ops.text: Insurance. MSL shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than U.S. $1,000,000 per occurrence and U.S. $2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than U.S. $2,000,000; where MSL processes data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than U.S. $5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. MSL shall provide certificates of insurance to IBM on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 16.22 (Insurance) in the GENERAL article requiring MSL to carry CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy and workers' compensation coverage and to provide certificates on request.

quote: MSL will provide replacement value insurance coverage for consigned Products. IBM will be named as a joint insured with respect to consigned Products for its interest.
rationale: The Agreement contains no vendor insurance article. The only insurance references are asset-specific: replacement-value cover for consigned Products with IBM as joint insured (§13.1(b), p0909), IBM-owned tooling insurance carried by IBM (§21.2, p1107), and freight/NIC insurance built into price (§10.5, p0863; Attachment 1 §1.15, p0649). None of these provides commercial general liability, professional (E&O), cyber/privacy or workers' compensation cover, nor certificates on request. MSL is an outsourcing vendor that holds our consigned inventory, occupies leased premises and accesses our I/T systems, so the fallback (E&O and cyber) is not met either. We therefore insert a short Section 16.22 at the preferred level in the GENERAL article, with the cyber trigger drafted to reach all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "MSL shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than U.S. $1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same sentence: "and U.S. $2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than U.S. $2,000,000".

elements.evidence: "where MSL processes data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than U.S. $5,000,000" — trigger covers every category of Customer data rather than selected named types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall provide certificates of insurance to IBM on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of not less than U.S. $2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1M fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of not less than U.S. $5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2M fallback floor.

verification.notes: All six preferred elements appear in a single inserted insurance paragraph with the exact limits, bases (per occurrence / aggregate), the conditional cyber trigger, workers' compensation and certificates on request; the preferred level is complete. The fallback floors are independently satisfied by the same inserted limits. Minimality: the insertion is a concise new clause for a genuinely missing obligation. The drafter omitted the model language's optional extras ("at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail), which would have been non-minimal; no wording outside the checklist was added and no existing text was deleted or paraphrased. Intent preserved: the asset-specific insurance provisions (§13.1(b) consigned-Product replacement-value cover with IBM as joint insured, §21.2 IBM-owned tooling) remain intact and do not contradict the new general coverage requirement; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced. Minor note only (not a defect): the clause does not state a duration/term anchor for the coverage, but no selected element requires one.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
mappings.quote: b) The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to

mappings.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
Gross negligence is uncapped.
Wilful misconduct is uncapped.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We re-based the mutual cap on twelve months' fees rather than 3% of bill-of-materials value, which is far below our fallback floor, and added the standard carve-outs so indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct sit outside the cap.

ops.newText: is limited to the fees paid or payable by IBM under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.
ops.oldText: is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.

ops.text: c) The limitation in Subsection 15.3(b) does not apply to a Party's indemnification obligations, breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or willful misconduct.

proposal.summary: Re-base the mutual cap in 15.3(b) on twelve months' fees and add carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct.

quote: b) The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
rationale: Section 15.3(b) is mutual, but the cap basis is 3% of the bill-of-materials value of Products delivered — a small fraction of the fees IBM pays MSL and well below the fallback floor of 12 months' fees. There are no carve-outs anywhere in Section 15: MSL's indemnity in 15.1 (infringement, legal non-compliance, warranty failure), the confidentiality obligations in 13.2, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside this cap with no super-cap, which is walk-away territory. The mutual consequential/lost-profits waiver in 15.3(a) is acceptable. The $25,000 limit in the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement Section 15 caps IBM's own exposure and is not flagged. We therefore target the fallback: keep the mutual cap, re-base it on twelve months' fees, and add one carve-out sentence.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

checks.name: cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor
no unlimited Customer liability language remains

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b): "The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to..." — the cap runs to both IBM and MSL; the pre-existing mutuality was retained.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b) caps at "the fees paid or payable by IBM under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" only; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To reach preferred, add "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 15.3(a): "Neither Party will be liable to the other for lost profits, consequential, punitive, or incidental damages" — bilateral; "indirect" is not expressly named but consequential/incidental damages are excluded on both sides.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c): "The limitation in Subsection 15.3(b) does not apply to a Party's ... breach of its confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in Section 15.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c): "does not apply to a Party's indemnification obligations", which lifts MSL's 15.1 indemnity out of the cap.

elements.element: Gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) expressly excludes "gross negligence" from the 15.3(b) limitation.

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) expressly excludes "willful misconduct" from the 15.3(b) limitation.

elements.element: Fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is absent from the new 15.3(c) carve-out list; add "fraud" to the excluded claims to reach preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in rendered 15.3(c); only the indemnification obligations are excluded, which does not expressly cover direct infringement claims of the other party's IP.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in rendered 15.3 states that IBM's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to the cap; no such sentence was added.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b) applies "for either Party", and no residual language leaves IBM's liability unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b) now reads "limited to the fees paid or payable by IBM under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim", replacing the 3%-of-bill-of-materials basis.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c): "The limitation in Subsection 15.3(b) does not apply to a Party's indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) carves out "breach of its confidentiality obligations", placing the Section 13.2 duties outside the cap.

elements.element: Gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) carves out "gross negligence".

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) carves out "willful misconduct".

verification.notes: Position-complete at the fallback: the cap remains mutual, is re-based on twelve months of fees paid or payable by IBM, and the single new subsection (c) supplies exactly the four fallback carve-outs (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct). Preferred is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP, and no statement that IBM's payment obligations are outside the capped damages. Minimality holds: only the cap basis in 15.3(b) was replaced and one carve-out sentence added; the favourable mutual consequential/punitive/incidental waiver in 15.3(a) and the mutual framing of (b) are retained, and no survival tails, expense language, or extra damages categories were bolted on. Intent preserved: the cross-reference in new (c) points correctly to Subsection 15.3(b); the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement $25,000 limit and the Section 15.1 indemnity mechanics are untouched and not contradicted. Drafting caveat (not a defect): "fees" is lower-case and undefined in this manufacturing/outsourcing context where IBM pays Product prices; consider "amounts paid or payable by IBM for Products and Services" if MSL argues purchase prices are not "fees". Optional uplift toward preferred in negotiation: append "fraud", "breach of data protection or security obligations" and "infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights" to 15.3(c), and add the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor.
